785	def _parse_spdx(document: dict) -> tuple[set[_Identity], set[_Edge]]:
786	    """Validate an SPDX 2.3 JSON document and return (identities, edges)."""
787	    if document.get("spdxVersion") != "SPDX-2.3":
788	        raise ValueError("spdxVersion 必须为 SPDX-2.3")
789	    document_spdxid = document.get("SPDXID")
790	    if not isinstance(document_spdxid, str) or not document_spdxid:
791	        raise ValueError("文档 SPDXID 必须为非空字符串")
792	    if "packages" not in document:
793	        raise ValueError("缺少 packages 字段")
794	    packages = document["packages"]
795	    if not isinstance(packages, list):
796	        raise ValueError("packages 必须为数组")
797	
798	    graph = _SbomGraph()
799	    for index, package in enumerate(packages):
800	        if not isinstance(package, dict):
801	            raise ValueError(f"packages[{index}] 必须为对象")
802	        spdxid = package.get("SPDXID")
803	        if not isinstance(spdxid, str) or not spdxid:
804	            raise ValueError(f"packages[{index}] SPDXID 必须为非空字符串")
805	        if spdxid == document_spdxid:
806	            raise ValueError(f"packages[{index}] SPDXID 与文档标识冲突: {spdxid}")
807	        graph.ensure_unique(spdxid, f"SPDXID 重复: {spdxid}")
808	        identity = _spdx_purl_identity(package, index, spdxid)
809	        if "versionInfo" in package:
810	            _check_declared_version(
811	                package["versionInfo"],
812	                identity[2],
813	                f"packages[{index}] (SPDXID {spdxid}) versionInfo",
814	            )
815	        graph.register(spdxid, identity)
816	
817	    relationships = document.get("relationships", [])
818	    if not isinstance(relationships, list):
819	        raise ValueError("relationships 必须为数组")
820	    for index, relationship in enumerate(relationships):
821	        if not isinstance(relationship, dict):
822	            raise ValueError(f"relationships[{index}] 必须为对象")
823	        relationship_type = relationship.get("relationshipType")
824	        if relationship_type == "DEPENDS_ON":
825	            source_key, target_key = "spdxElementId", "relatedSpdxElement"
826	        elif relationship_type == "DEPENDENCY_OF":
827	            source_key, target_key = "relatedSpdxElement", "spdxElementId"
828	        else:
829	            # DESCRIBES and every other non-dependency relation are ignored;
830	            # the document itself is never a component.
831	            continue
832	        source = relationship.get(source_key)
833	        target = relationship.get(target_key)
834	        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
835	            raise ValueError(
836	                f"relationships[{index}].{source_key} 必须为非空字符串"
837	            )
838	        if not isinstance(target, str) or not target:
839	            raise ValueError(
840	                f"relationships[{index}].{target_key} 必须为非空字符串"
841	            )
842	        if source == document_spdxid or target == document_spdxid:
843	            raise ValueError(
844	                f"relationships[{index}] 引用了文档标识而非包: {source} -> {target}"
845	            )
846	        dependent = graph.identity_of(
847	            source, f"relationships[{index}] 引用未知标识: {source}"
848	        )
849	        dependency = graph.identity_of(
850	            target, f"relationships[{index}] 引用未知标识: {target}"
851	        )
852	        graph.add_edge(dependent, dependency, (source, target))
853	
854	    return graph.result()

857	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
858	# Retention rule — the single decision shared by SBOM source replacement
859	# (import_sbom) and manual-dependency revocation (remove_dependency).
860	#
861	# Both operations remove declarations and then have to decide which catalog
862	# entities actually leave. Keeping that judgment in exactly these two
863	# predicates (and reconciling through one Catalog method) means adjusting the
864	# rule once covers both operations; the decision can never drift between a
865	# re-import and a remove-dependency.
866	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
867	
868	# A relationship is retained while it keeps any basis: a manual registration
869	# OR a declaration by at least one SBOM source. Revoking the manual entry
870	# therefore leaves a source-declared relationship in place, and vice versa.
871	# Outer columns are qualified with the real table name so the same predicate is
872	# valid inside DELETE, SELECT and EXISTS scopes alike.
873	_RELATION_RETAINED_PREDICATE = (
874	    "dependencies.manual = 1 OR EXISTS ("
875	    "SELECT 1 FROM dependency_sources ds "
876	    "WHERE ds.dependency_id = dependencies.id)"
877	)
878	
879	# A component is retained while it keeps any basis: a manual registration, a
880	# declaration by at least one source, OR being an endpoint of a manually
881	# registered relationship (the anchor that keeps the two ends a surviving
882	# manual edge needs). When all three bases vanish the component is deleted.
883	# Only *manual* edges anchor endpoints: an edge a source alone declares always
884	# has both ends declared by that same source, so it never has to hold an
885	# endpoint on its own. Components are judged independently, so one endpoint
886	# leaving never blocks or cascades to the other or to anything connected to it.
887	_COMPONENT_RETAINED_PREDICATE = (
888	    "components.manual = 1 OR EXISTS ("
889	    "SELECT 1 FROM component_sources cs "
890	    "WHERE cs.component_id = components.id) "
891	    "OR EXISTS ("
892	    "SELECT 1 FROM dependencies d WHERE d.manual = 1 "
893	    "AND (d.dependent_id = components.id OR d.dependency_id = components.id))"
894	)

897	class Catalog:
898	    def __init__(self, database: str | Path = ":memory:") -> None:
899	        self.connection = sqlite3.connect(str(database))
900	        self.connection.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
901	        # Let concurrent writers wait for each other; guarded UPDATEs still
902	        # ensure that two processes processing one request produce at most a
903	        # single state change.
904	        self.connection.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout = 10000")
905	        self.connection.executescript(SCHEMA)
906	        self._migrate()
907	
908	    def _migrate(self) -> None:
909	        """Add ownership columns to databases created by earlier releases.
910	
911	        Components and relationships already present are considered manually
912	        registered, so they survive source replacement.
913	        """
914	        component_columns = {
915	            str(row["name"])
916	            for row in self.connection.execute("PRAGMA table_info(components)")
917	        }
918	        if "manual" not in component_columns:
919	            self.connection.execute(
920	                "ALTER TABLE components ADD COLUMN manual INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0"
921	            )
922	            self.connection.execute("UPDATE components SET manual = 1")
923	        dependency_columns = {
924	            str(row["name"])
925	            for row in self.connection.execute("PRAGMA table_info(dependencies)")
926	        }
927	        if "manual" not in dependency_columns:
928	            self.connection.execute(
929	                "ALTER TABLE dependencies ADD COLUMN manual INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0"
930	            )
931	            self.connection.execute("UPDATE dependencies SET manual = 1")
932	        self.connection.commit()
933	
934	    def close(self) -> None:
935	        self.connection.close()
936	
937	    @contextmanager
938	    def _write_tx(self):
939	        """A serialized write transaction.
940	
941	        ``BEGIN IMMEDIATE`` takes the database write lock up front, so two
942	        concurrent processes serialize their check-then-write sequences: the
943	        second blocks until the first commits and then observes its changes.
944	        Used for exemption requests and decisions to guarantee that a scope
945	        never gets two live requests and that a request changes state at most
946	        once.
947	        """
948	        self.connection.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
949	        try:
950	            yield
951	        except Exception:
952	            self.connection.rollback()
953	            raise
954	        else:
955	            self.connection.commit()
956	
957	    def add_component(
958	        self, service: str, ecosystem: str, name: str, version: str
959	    ) -> None:
960	        values = tuple(value.strip() for value in (service, ecosystem, name, version))
961	        if any(not value for value in values):
962	            raise ValueError("component fields must not be empty")
963	        with self.connection:
964	            self.connection.execute(
965	                "INSERT INTO components(service, ecosystem, name, version, manual) "
966	                "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 1) "
967	                "ON CONFLICT(service, ecosystem, name, version) DO UPDATE SET manual = 1",
968	                values,
969	            )

971	    def add_vulnerability(self, identifier: str, component_name: str, severity: str) -> None:
972	        identifier, component_name, severity = (
973	            identifier.strip(),
974	            component_name.strip(),
975	            severity.strip().lower(),
976	        )
977	        if not identifier or not component_name:
978	            raise ValueError("vulnerability identity must not be empty")
979	        if severity not in {"low", "medium", "high", "critical"}:
980	            raise ValueError("unsupported severity")

982	            self.connection.execute(
983	                "INSERT INTO vulnerabilities(id, component_name, severity) VALUES (?, ?, ?) "
984	                "ON CONFLICT(id, component_name) DO UPDATE SET severity=excluded.severity",
985	                (identifier, component_name, severity),

1002	    def add_dependency(
1003	        self,
1004	        service: str,
1005	        ecosystem: str,
1006	        name: str,
1007	        version: str,
1008	        dependency_service: str,
1009	        dependency_ecosystem: str,
1010	        dependency_name: str,
1011	        dependency_version: str,
1012	    ) -> None:
1013	        dependent = tuple(value.strip() for value in (service, ecosystem, name, version))
1014	        dependency = tuple(
1015	            value.strip()
1016	            for value in (
1017	                dependency_service,
1018	                dependency_ecosystem,
1019	                dependency_name,
1020	                dependency_version,
1021	            )
1022	        )
1023	        if any(not value for value in dependent + dependency):
1024	            raise ValueError("dependency fields must not be empty")
1025	        if dependent == dependency:

1049	    def _reconcile_retention(
1050	        self,
1051	        candidate_dependency_ids: set[int] | None = None,
1052	        candidate_component_ids: set[int] | tuple[int, ...] | None = None,
1053	    ) -> tuple[int, int]:
1054	        """Apply the one retention rule after declarations were removed.
1055	
1056	        This is the only place that deletes entities for having lost every
1057	        reason to stay, so ``import_sbom`` (source replacement) and
1058	        ``remove_dependency`` (manual revocation) can never disagree:
1059	
1060	        * a relationship leaves only when it is neither manually registered
1061	          nor declared by any remaining source;
1062	        * a component leaves only when it is not manually registered, is
1063	          declared by no remaining source, and is not an endpoint of any
1064	          surviving manually registered relationship.
1065	
1066	        Relationships are reconciled first, so a relationship that loses its
1067	        last basis releases the endpoints it was anchoring. Components are
1068	        then judged independently against the surviving relationships — one
1069	        endpoint leaving never blocks or cascades to the other, or to any
1070	        connected component.
1071	
1072	        The candidate sets bound which entities may be deleted. ``None`` means
1073	        "every entity" (a source replacement can affect the whole catalog); a
1074	        targeted operation passes just the edge and the two endpoints it
1075	        touched, so revoking one relationship can never sweep unrelated
1076	        entities. The bound is only a scope: the two retention predicates are
1077	        still what decides each candidate.
1078	
1079	        Returns ``(deleted_components, deleted_dependencies)`` counting the
1080	        rows that actually left, so a source merely losing one declaration
1081	        while the entity stays (another source/manual basis remains) is never
1082	        counted as a deletion.
1083	        """
1084	        if candidate_dependency_ids is None:
1085	            dependency_scope = ""
1086	            dependency_params: tuple = ()
1087	        else:
1088	            placeholders = ", ".join("?" for _ in candidate_dependency_ids)
1089	            dependency_scope = f" AND id IN ({placeholders})"
1090	            dependency_params = tuple(sorted(candidate_dependency_ids))
1091	        deleted_dependency_cursor = self.connection.execute(
1092	            f"DELETE FROM dependencies "
1093	            f"WHERE NOT ({_RELATION_RETAINED_PREDICATE}){dependency_scope}",
1094	            dependency_params,
1095	        )
1096	        deleted_dependency_count = deleted_dependency_cursor.rowcount
1097	
1098	        if candidate_component_ids is None:
1099	            component_scope = ""
1100	            component_params: tuple = ()
1101	        else:
1102	            placeholders = ", ".join("?" for _ in candidate_component_ids)
1103	            component_scope = f" AND id IN ({placeholders})"
1104	            component_params = tuple(candidate_component_ids)
1105	        deleted_component_cursor = self.connection.execute(
1106	            f"DELETE FROM components "
1107	            f"WHERE NOT ({_COMPONENT_RETAINED_PREDICATE}){component_scope}",
1108	            component_params,
1109	        )
1110	        deleted_component_count = deleted_component_cursor.rowcount
1111	        return deleted_component_count, deleted_dependency_count

1113	    def remove_dependency(
1114	        self,
1115	        service: str,
1116	        ecosystem: str,
1117	        name: str,
1118	        version: str,
1119	        dependency_service: str,
1120	        dependency_ecosystem: str,
1121	        dependency_name: str,
1122	        dependency_version: str,
1123	    ) -> None:
1124	        dependent = tuple(value.strip() for value in (service, ecosystem, name, version))
1125	        dependency = tuple(
1126	            value.strip()
1127	            for value in (
1128	                dependency_service,
1129	                dependency_ecosystem,
1130	                dependency_name,
1131	                dependency_version,
1132	            )
1133	        )
1134	        if any(not value for value in dependent + dependency):
1135	            raise ValueError("dependency fields must not be empty")
1136	        dependent_id = self._component_id(*dependent)
1137	        dependency_id = self._component_id(*dependency)
1138	        if dependent_id is None or dependency_id is None:
1139	            # Nothing targeted: succeed without touching the catalog.
1140	            return
1141	        edge_row = self.connection.execute(
1142	            "SELECT id FROM dependencies "
1143	            "WHERE dependent_id = ? AND dependency_id = ?",
1144	            (dependent_id, dependency_id),
1145	        ).fetchone()
1146	        if edge_row is None:
1147	            # The two components exist but this relationship does not. Succeed
1148	            # without changing anything: revoking a non-existent manual
1149	            # registration must not be a way to sweep the endpoints (or any
1150	            # other component) through the cleanup rule.
1151	            return
1152	        edge_id = int(edge_row["id"])
1153	        with self.connection:
1154	            # Only revoke the manual registration; relationships still declared
1155	            # by an imported source continue to participate in impact queries.
1156	            self.connection.execute(
1157	                "UPDATE dependencies SET manual = 0 WHERE id = ?",
1158	                (edge_id,),
1159	            )
1160	            # Reapply the single retention rule, scoped to exactly this edge
1161	            # and its two endpoints: the revoked edge may leave if no source
1162	            # still declares it, and each end is then judged on its own. The
1163	            # scope guarantees one end leaving never removes the other or any
1164	            # connected component, and that unrelated entities are untouched.
1165	            self._reconcile_retention(
1166	                candidate_dependency_ids={edge_id},
1167	                candidate_component_ids={dependent_id, dependency_id},
1168	            )

1170	    def import_sbom(
1171	        self, service: str, source_name: str, sbom: object
1172	    ) -> ImportResult:
1173	        """Register the components and dependencies of an SBOM document.
1174	
1175	        Both CycloneDX 1.5 and SPDX 2.3 JSON are accepted; the format is
1176	        detected automatically.
1177	
1178	        The source (service, source_name) is replaced: its previous components
1179	        and relationships lose ownership, and components/relationships no
1180	        longer owned by any source or manually registered are deleted. The
1181	        whole list is validated before any write, so failures leave the
1182	        catalog untouched.
1183	        """
1184	        service = service.strip()
1185	        source_name = source_name.strip()
1186	        if not service or not source_name:
1187	            raise ValueError("service 和 source 名称不能为空")
1188	        identities, edges = _parse_sbom(sbom)
1189	
1190	        with self.connection:
1191	            source_row = self.connection.execute(
1192	                "SELECT id FROM sources WHERE service = ? AND name = ?",
1193	                (service, source_name),
1194	            ).fetchone()
1195	            if source_row is None:
1196	                source_id = int(
1197	                    self.connection.execute(
1198	                        "INSERT INTO sources(service, name) VALUES (?, ?)",
1199	                        (service, source_name),
1200	                    ).lastrowid
1201	                )
1202	            else:
1203	                source_id = int(source_row["id"])
1204	
1205	            # Drop the previous ownership of this source.
1206	            self.connection.execute(
1207	                "DELETE FROM component_sources WHERE source_id = ?", (source_id,)
1208	            )
1209	            self.connection.execute(
1210	                "DELETE FROM dependency_sources WHERE source_id = ?", (source_id,)
1211	            )
1212	
1213	            added_components = 0
1214	            component_ids: dict[tuple[str, str, str], int] = {}
1215	            for ecosystem, name, version in sorted(identities):
1216	                row = self.connection.execute(
1217	                    "SELECT id FROM components "
1218	                    "WHERE service = ? AND ecosystem = ? AND name = ? AND version = ?",
1219	                    (service, ecosystem, name, version),
1220	                ).fetchone()
1221	                if row is None:
1222	                    component_id = int(
1223	                        self.connection.execute(
1224	                            "INSERT INTO components(service, ecosystem, name, version, manual) "
1225	                            "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 0)",
1226	                            (service, ecosystem, name, version),
1227	                        ).lastrowid
1228	                    )
1229	                    added_components += 1
1230	                else:
1231	                    component_id = int(row["id"])
1232	                component_ids[(ecosystem, name, version)] = component_id
1233	                self.connection.execute(
1234	                    "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO component_sources(component_id, source_id) "
1235	                    "VALUES (?, ?)",
1236	                    (component_id, source_id),
1237	                )
1238	
1239	            added_dependencies = 0
1240	            for dependent_identity, dependency_identity in sorted(edges):
1241	                dependent_id = component_ids[dependent_identity]
1242	                dependency_id = component_ids[dependency_identity]
1243	                row = self.connection.execute(
1244	                    "SELECT id FROM dependencies "
1245	                    "WHERE dependent_id = ? AND dependency_id = ?",
1246	                    (dependent_id, dependency_id),
1247	                ).fetchone()
1248	                if row is None:
1249	                    dependency_row_id = int(
1250	                        self.connection.execute(
1251	                            "INSERT INTO dependencies(dependent_id, dependency_id, manual) "
1252	                            "VALUES (?, ?, 0)",
1253	                            (dependent_id, dependency_id),
1254	                        ).lastrowid
1255	                    )
1256	                    added_dependencies += 1
1257	                else:
1258	                    dependency_row_id = int(row["id"])
1259	                self.connection.execute(
1260	                    "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO dependency_sources(dependency_id, source_id) "
1261	                    "VALUES (?, ?)",
1262	                    (dependency_row_id, source_id),
1263	                )
1264	
1265	            # Reapply the single retention rule after this source's ownership
1266	            # was withdrawn and the new declaration recorded. Scope is the
1267	            # whole catalog: any relationship no longer manually registered
1268	            # and declared by no source leaves, and any component that has
1269	            # likewise lost all three bases follows (independently per
1270	            # component). The returned counts count rows that actually leave,
1271	            # so a source merely withdrawing one declaration while another
1272	            # source or a manual registration keeps the entity is not a
1273	            # deletion. remove_dependency runs the exact same rule.
1274	            deleted_components, deleted_dependencies = self._reconcile_retention()

1276	        return ImportResult(
1277	            source_components=len(identities),
1278	            added_components=added_components,
1279	            deleted_components=deleted_components,
1280	            added_dependencies=added_dependencies,
1281	            deleted_dependencies=deleted_dependencies,
1282	        )

1384	    def _direct_hits(
1385	        self, components: dict[int, dict[str, str]]
1386	    ) -> dict[tuple[str | None, str, str], dict[int, dict]]:
1387	        """Find the components directly hit by every vulnerability kind.
1388	
1389	        Returns a mapping from an impact-group key
1390	        ``(source, vulnerability id, matched package)`` — ``source`` is None
1391	        for a manually registered vulnerability and the source name for an
1392	        imported OSV record — to a mapping of directly hit component ids to
1393	        the hit description recorded at that terminal: ``severity``,
1394	        ``severity_basis`` and ``matched_conditions``.
1395	
1396	        Manual observations hit components by their verbatim package name and
1397	        carry no version conditions or severity basis. OSV records match on
1398	        the normalized PyPI package name and on the union of explicit
1399	        versions and ECOSYSTEM ranges compared with PEP 440; a candidate
1400	        component whose version cannot be parsed is a query error that
1401	        points out the component. Gathering both kinds here lets dependency
1402	        propagation, path selection and record generation share one code
1403	        path.
1404	        """
1405	        groups: dict[tuple[str | None, str, str], dict[int, dict]] = {}
1406	
1407	        for observation in self.connection.execute(
1408	            "SELECT id, component_name, severity FROM vulnerabilities"
1409	        ):
1410	            matched_name = str(observation["component_name"])
1411	            key = (None, str(observation["id"]), matched_name)
1412	            detail = {
1413	                "severity": str(observation["severity"]),
1414	                "severity_basis": None,
1415	                "matched_conditions": None,
1416	            }
1417	            terminals = groups.setdefault(key, {})
1418	            for component_id, component in components.items():
1419	                if component["name"] == matched_name:
1420	                    terminals[component_id] = detail
1421	
1422	        records = self._osv_records()
1423	        if records:
1424	            by_package: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
1425	            for record in records:
1426	                by_package.setdefault(record["package_name"], []).append(record)
1427	
1428	            for component_id, component in components.items():
1429	                if component["ecosystem"] != "pypi":
1430	                    continue
1431	                normalized = normalize_pypi_name(component["name"])
1432	                candidates = by_package.get(normalized)
1433	                if candidates is None:
1434	                    continue
1435	                try:
1436	                    version = Version(component["version"])
1437	                except InvalidVersion as error:
1438	                    raise ValueError(
1439	                        f"组件 {component['service']}/{component['ecosystem']}/"
1440	                        f"{component['name']}/{component['version']} 版本无法解析"
1441	                    ) from error
1442	                for record in candidates:
1443	                    matched_conditions = [
1444	                        _format_condition(condition)
1445	                        for condition in record["conditions"]
1446	                        if _condition_matches(condition, version)
1447	                    ]
1448	                    if matched_conditions:
1449	                        key = (record["source"], record["id"], normalized)
1450	                        groups.setdefault(key, {})[component_id] = {
1451	                            "severity": record["severity"],
1452	                            "severity_basis": (
1453	                                "default"
1454	                                if record["severity_default"]
1455	                                else "declared"
1456	                            ),
1457	                            "matched_conditions": matched_conditions,
1458	                        }
1459	        return groups

1524	    @staticmethod
1525	    def _reconstruct_path(
1526	        component_id: int,
1527	        distance: dict[int, int],
1528	        forward: dict[int, list[int]],
1529	        components: dict[int, dict[str, str]],
1530	    ) -> list[int]:
1531	        """Reconstruct the shortest path, ties broken by component identity."""
1532	        path_ids = [component_id]
1533	        while distance[path_ids[-1]] > 0:
1534	            current = path_ids[-1]
1535	            candidates = [
1536	                nxt
1537	                for nxt in forward.get(current, ())
1538	                if distance.get(nxt) == distance[current] - 1
1539	            ]
1540	            path_ids.append(
1541	                min(
1542	                    candidates,
1543	                    key=lambda nxt: Catalog._component_identity_key(
1544	                        components[nxt]
1545	                    ),
1546	                )
1547	            )
1548	        return path_ids

1550	    @staticmethod
1551	    def _propagate_distances(
1552	        terminals: dict[int, dict],
1553	        reverse: dict[int, list[int]],
1554	        bounds: frozenset[int] | set[int] | None = None,
1555	    ) -> dict[int, int]:
1556	        """Fewest dependency hops from each component to a directly hit one.
1557	
1558	        Multi-source BFS over the reverse dependency edges starting from all
1559	        directly hit components of one vulnerability/source/package group.
1560	        When ``bounds`` is given, only components inside it receive a
1561	        distance — this is the single propagation rule used by both the
1562	        directory/service-wide query (no bounds: every component the group
1563	        reaches) and the full-identity query (bounds = the target's forward
1564	        dependency closure). Restricting the BFS leaves every distance
1565	        inside the closure identical to the unbounded run. Cycles are
1566	        handled by the distance map, so every component is visited at most
1567	        once and a path never repeats a component.
1568	        """
1569	        distance: dict[int, int] = {}
1570	        for component_id in sorted(terminals):
1571	            if bounds is None or component_id in bounds:
1572	                distance[component_id] = 0
1573	        queue = deque(distance)
1574	        while queue:
1575	            node = queue.popleft()
1576	            for dependent in reverse.get(node, ()):
1577	                if bounds is not None and dependent not in bounds:
1578	                    continue
1579	                if dependent not in distance:
1580	                    distance[dependent] = distance[node] + 1
1581	                    queue.append(dependent)
1582	        return distance

1584	    def _impact_record(
1585	        self,
1586	        components: dict[int, dict[str, str]],
1587	        group_key: tuple[str | None, str, str],
1588	        terminals: dict[int, dict],
1589	        component_id: int,
1590	        distance: dict[int, int],
1591	        forward: dict[int, list[int]],
1592	    ) -> dict:
1593	        """Build the one impact record of a component within one hit group.
1594	
1595	        This is the single record-construction rule shared by the
1596	        directory-wide, service-scoped and full-identity queries, so the
1597	        direct/indirect flag, the dependency path, the source, the severity
1598	        and its basis and the matched version conditions can never be

            for dependent in reverse.get(node, ()):
                if dependent not in affected:
                    affected.add(dependent)
                    queue.append(dependent)
        return affected

    def _affected_ids(self) -> set[int]:
        _, _, reverse, direct_groups = self._impact_graph()
        return self._affected_ids_from_groups(direct_groups, reverse)

    def summary(self) -> Summary:
        _, _, reverse, direct_groups = self._impact_graph()
        affected = self._affected_ids_from_groups(direct_groups, reverse)

        # Manual observations and OSV hits share the direct-hit model; only
        # groups with at least one directly hit component participate.
        manual_severities: list[str] = []
        osv_pairs: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
        osv_severities: list[str] = []
        for (source, identifier, matched_name), terminals in direct_groups.items():
            if not terminals:
                continue
            if source is None:
                # One manual vulnerability row per group; its severity is the
                # same at every directly hit component.
                manual_severities.append(next(iter(terminals.values()))["severity"])
            else:
                # Imported vulnerabilities are deduplicated by id and
                # normalized package name across sources, and only records
                # that actually hit a component count.
                osv_pairs.add((identifier, matched_name))
                osv_severities.extend(
                    detail["severity"] for detail in terminals.values()
                )

        row = self.connection.execute(
            "SELECT COUNT(*) AS components FROM components"
        ).fetchone()

        highest: str | None = None
        for severity in manual_severities + osv_severities:
            if highest is None or SEVERITY_RANK[severity] > SEVERITY_RANK[highest]:
                highest = severity

        return Summary(
            components=int(row["components"]),
            affected_components=len(affected),
            vulnerabilities=len(manual_severities) + len(osv_pairs),
            highest_severity=highest,
        )

    def affected_services(self) -> list[str]:
        affected = self._affected_ids()
        if not affected:
            return []
        placeholders = ", ".join("?" for _ in affected)
        rows = self.connection.execute(
            f"SELECT DISTINCT service FROM components WHERE id IN ({placeholders}) "
            "ORDER BY service",
            sorted(affected),
        )
        return [str(row["service"]) for row in rows]

    def impact(
        self,
        service: str | None = None,
        ecosystem: str | None = None,
        name: str | None = None,
        version: str | None = None,
    ) -> list[dict]:
        identity_filter = (ecosystem, name, version)
        if any(value is not None for value in identity_filter):
            if not all(value is not None for value in identity_filter):
                raise ValueError(
                    "ecosystem, name and version must be provided together"
                )
            if service is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    "service is required when filtering by component identity"
                )

        if all(value is not None for value in identity_filter):
            # A full identity resolves exactly one component. The graph is
            # still built first (including OSV version matching for the whole
            # service), so a bad version in the service fails this query even
            # when the target does not exist; afterwards propagation is
            # bounded by the target's forward closure and only its own paths
            # are materialized. On a long chain this keeps memory growing
            # with the service graph and the returned paths instead of the
            # paths of every other affected component.
            components, forward, reverse, direct_groups = self._impact_graph(
                service
            )
            target_id = self._component_id(service, ecosystem, name, version)
            if target_id is None:
                records = []
            else:
                reachable = self._forward_reachable(target_id, forward)
                records = self._impact_records(
                    service,
                    target_id=target_id,
                    reachable=reachable,
                    components=components,
                    forward=forward,
                    reverse=reverse,
                    direct_groups=direct_groups,
                )
        else:
            # Build the graph within the service scope up front, so components
            # of other services never take part in OSV version matching or
            # dependency propagation.
            records = self._impact_records(service)

        records.sort(key=_impact_sort_key)
        return records

    def _impact_records(
        self,
        service: str | None = None,
        target_id: int | None = None,
        reachable: frozenset[int] | set[int] | None = None,
        components: dict[int, dict[str, str]] | None = None,
        forward: dict[int, list[int]] | None = None,
        reverse: dict[int, list[int]] | None = None,
        direct_groups: dict[tuple[str | None, str, str], dict[int, dict]]
        | None = None,
    ) -> list[dict]:
        """Current impact records, in an unspecified order.

        One record per (component, vulnerability, source, matched package),
        for both manual observations (``source`` None, no version conditions
        and no severity basis) and named OSV sources (normalized PyPI package
        match, terminal version conditions and a declared/default severity
        basis). Propagation, shortest-path selection, terminal conditions and
        record construction run through exactly one set of rules here, so the
        directory-wide, service-scoped and full-identity queries can never
        explain the same component differently.

        When ``service`` is given, matching and propagation run only over that
        service's graph; components in other services never participate, so a
        component with an unparseable version in another service cannot make
        this service's query fail.

        When ``target_id`` is given, ``reachable`` (the target's forward
        dependency closure) bounds propagation to exactly the components the
        target can reach, and only the target's own record per group is built.
        Every distance and path inside the closure is computed by the same
        rules as the unbounded run, so the returned records are identical to
        the corresponding records of a service-wide query, while memory grows
        with the service graph and the returned paths instead of with the
        materialized paths of every other affected component. A preloaded
        graph (``components``/``forward``/``reverse``/``direct_groups``) is
        reused when supplied, so the caller can resolve the target after the
        whole-service graph — including OSV version matching — was built.
        """
        if components is None:
            components, forward, reverse, direct_groups = self._impact_graph(
                service
            )
        if target_id is not None and target_id not in components:
            return []

        records: list[dict] = []
        for group_key, terminals in direct_groups.items():
            if not terminals:
                continue
            # Multi-source BFS over reverse edges: distance = fewest
            # dependency hops from an affected component to a directly hit
            # one. All directly hit components of the group are distance 0
            # (inside the target's closure when bounded), so a component
            # reached by several paths gets one record and propagation
            # through cycles terminates at visited nodes.
            distance = self._propagate_distances(terminals, reverse, reachable)
            if target_id is None:
                affected_ids = sorted(distance)
            elif target_id not in distance:
                # No directly hit component lies downstream of the target in
                # this group, or the target cannot reach one: no record.
                continue
            else:
                affected_ids = [target_id]
            for component_id in affected_ids:
                records.append(
                    self._impact_record(
                        components,
                        group_key,
                        terminals,
                        component_id,
                        distance,
                        forward,
                    )
                )

        return records

    @staticmethod
    def _forward_reachable(
        target_id: int, forward: dict[int, list[int]]
    ) -> frozenset[int]:
        """All components reachable from ``target_id`` along dependency edges.

        The closure depends only on the graph, never on a particular
        vulnerability group, so it is computed once per full-identity query
        and reused as the propagation bound for every group. Cycles
        terminate through the visited set.
        """
        reachable = {target_id}
        queue = deque([target_id])
        while queue:
            node = queue.popleft()
            for dependency in forward.get(node, ()):
                if dependency not in reachable:
                    reachable.add(dependency)
                    queue.append(dependency)
        return frozenset(reachable)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Vulnerability exemptions
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    @staticmethod
    def _clean_identity(
        service: object,
        ecosystem: object,
        name: object,
        version: object,
    ) -> tuple[str, str, str, str]:
        values = tuple(
            value.strip() if isinstance(value, str) else ""
            for value in (service, ecosystem, name, version)
        )
        if any(not value for value in values):
            raise ValueError("组件的 service、ecosystem、name、version 均不能为空")
        return values  # type: ignore[return-value]

    @staticmethod
    def _clean_text(value: object, context: str) -> str:
        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
            raise ValueError(f"{context}不能为空")
        return value.strip()

    @classmethod
    def _clean_scope(
        cls,
        service: object,
        ecosystem: object,
        name: object,
        version: object,
        vulnerability: object,
        matched_name: object,
        source: object,
    ) -> ScopeT:
        """Validate and trim one exemption-scope input into a canonical scope.

        Every external entry point (request submission) builds its scope
        here, so whitespace handling and the empty-field rules live in one
        place. An actual ``None`` source denotes a manually registered
        vulnerability; a provided source name is trimmed and names an OSV
        record. The two never collapse.
        """
        service, ecosystem, name, version = cls._clean_identity(
            service, ecosystem, name, version
        )
        vulnerability = cls._clean_text(vulnerability, "漏洞编号")
        matched_name = cls._clean_text(matched_name, "匹配包名")
        # Only an actual None denotes a manually registered vulnerability;
        # a provided but blank or non-string source stays an input error,
        # exactly as before — it must never silently become a manual scope.
        source_name = (
            None
            if source is None
            else cls._clean_text(source, "漏洞来源")
        )
        return (
            service, ecosystem, name, version,
            vulnerability, matched_name, source_name,
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _scope_from_row(row: sqlite3.Row) -> ScopeT:
        """Read the stored scope of one ``exemption_requests`` row.

        Stored rows are the only other source of scopes (approval
        re-checks, scope-occupation checks and report linking); building
        them here keeps stored scopes identical in shape and rules to
        freshly cleaned input scopes and to scopes of current records.
        """
        return tuple(
            None if field == "source" and row[field] is None
            else str(row[field])
            for field in _SCOPE_FIELDS
        )  # type: ignore[return-value]

    def _current_scope_impact(self, scope: ScopeT) -> dict | None:
        """The live impact record exactly matching ``scope``, if it exists now.

        This is the one existence/equality lookup shared by submission and
        approval: matching runs only inside the scope's target service, so a
        component with an unparseable version in another service neither
        fails the check nor is mistaken for the target, while the service's
        full dependency graph still participates — an upstream component
        reached only through dependencies counts as affected, and finding a
        same-named record without the dependency path does not. A version
        that has to be compared with an OSV record inside this service
        remains a query error (raised while the graph is built); the
        directly hit library and a component depending on it are different
        records, a manual ``None`` source never matches a named OSV source,
        and two named sources are judged independently.
        """
        for record in self._impact_records(scope[0]):
            if _scope_matches_record(scope, record):
                return record
        return None

    def request_exemption(
        self,
        request_id: str,
        service: str,
        ecosystem: str,
        name: str,
        version: str,
        vulnerability: str,
        matched_name: str,
        source: str | None,
        applicant: str,
        reason: str,
        expires_at: str | datetime,
        *,
        submitted_at: datetime | None = None,
    ) -> dict:
        """Apply to exempt one specific impact record.

        The scope is exactly (component identity, vulnerability id, matched
        package, source); ``source`` is None for a manually registered
        vulnerability and the source name for an imported OSV record. A retry
        with the same id and identical content confirms the original
        submission and returns the stored request exactly as it currently
        stands — its term, decision state and history are never altered, even
        when the retry happens at or after expiry, after the request was
        approved/rejected/revoked, or after the target impact disappeared. A
        reused id with any different content is rejected as a conflict. Only
        one live (pending or unexpired approved) request may exist per scope,
        and the expiry must be later than the submission instant only for a
        genuinely new request.
        """
        request_id = self._clean_text(request_id, "申请编号")
        # The scope is assembled exactly once through the shared cleaner; the
        # same seven-field tuple is what id confirmation, the existence
        # check, storage and scope occupation compare.
        scope = self._clean_scope(
            service, ecosystem, name, version,
            vulnerability, matched_name, source,
        )
        applicant = self._clean_text(applicant, "申请人")
        reason = self._clean_text(reason, "申请理由")

        if submitted_at is None:
            submitted_at = utc_now()
        elif submitted_at.tzinfo is None:
            raise ValueError("提交时刻必须带有时区信息")
        else:
            submitted_at = submitted_at.astimezone(timezone.utc)

        if isinstance(expires_at, datetime):
            expiry = expires_at
            if expiry.tzinfo is None:
                raise ValueError("到期时间必须带有时区信息")
            expiry = expiry.astimezone(timezone.utc)
        else:
            expiry = parse_timestamp(expires_at, "到期时间")

        with self._write_tx():
            existing = self.connection.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM exemption_requests WHERE id = ?", (request_id,)
            ).fetchone()
            if existing is not None:
                # An id names exactly one request for all time. Identical
                # content confirms the original submission and returns the
                # record exactly as it is now — no expiry check (the retry may
                # run at or after expiry), no impact-existence check (the
                # scope may have disappeared), no scope re-occupation, and no
                # change to the term, the approved severity or the history.
                # Any differing content is a conflict, never an overwrite.
                same_content = (
                    self._scope_from_row(existing) == scope
                    and str(existing["applicant"]) == applicant
                    and str(existing["reason"]) == reason
                    and str(existing["expires_at"]) == format_timestamp(expiry)
                )
                if not same_content:
                    raise ValueError(f"申请编号 {request_id!r} 已用于不同内容的申请")
                return self._fetch_request(request_id)

            # Everything below applies only to a genuinely new request id.
            if expiry <= submitted_at:
                raise ValueError("到期时间必须晚于提交时刻")

            if self._current_scope_impact(scope) is None:
                raise ValueError("申请目标不存在：当前没有匹配的漏洞影响记录")

            # No other live request may occupy the same scope.
            self._ensure_scope_open(scope, exclude_id=None, now=submitted_at)

            created = format_timestamp(submitted_at)
            self.connection.execute(
                """
                INSERT INTO exemption_requests(
                    id, service, ecosystem, name, version,
                    vulnerability, matched_name, source,
                    created_at, applicant, reason, expires_at, status
                ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
                """,
                (
                    request_id, *scope,
                    created, applicant, reason, format_timestamp(expiry),
                    EXEMPTION_PENDING,
                ),
            )
            self._append_event(
                request_id, submitted_at, applicant, "request", reason,
                None, EXEMPTION_PENDING,
            )
        return self._fetch_request(request_id)

    def _ensure_scope_open(
        self,
        scope: tuple,
        exclude_id: str | None,
        now: datetime,
    ) -> None:
        rows = self.connection.execute(
            """
            SELECT id, status, expires_at FROM exemption_requests
            WHERE service = ? AND ecosystem = ? AND name = ? AND version = ?
              AND vulnerability = ? AND matched_name = ?
              AND ((source IS NULL AND ? IS NULL) OR source = ?)
            """,
            (*scope[:6], scope[6], scope[6]),
        ).fetchall()
        now_text = format_timestamp(now)
        for row in rows:
            if str(row["id"]) == exclude_id:
                continue
            status = str(row["status"])
            if status not in EXEMPTION_OPEN:
                continue
            if str(row["expires_at"]) > now_text:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"同一范围已存在未到期的{_status_label(status)}申请: {row['id']}"
                )

    def _append_event(
        self,
        request_id: str,
        occurred_at: datetime,
        actor: str,
        action: str,
        reason: str,
        from_status: str | None,
        to_status: str,
    ) -> None:
        next_seq = self.connection.execute(
            "SELECT COALESCE(MAX(seq), 0) + 1 FROM exemption_events WHERE request_id = ?",
            (request_id,),
        ).fetchone()[0]
        self.connection.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO exemption_events(
                request_id, seq, occurred_at, actor, action, reason,
                from_status, to_status
            ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
            """,
            (
                request_id, int(next_seq), format_timestamp(occurred_at),
                actor, action, reason, from_status, to_status,
            ),
        )

    def _fetch_request(self, request_id: str) -> dict:
        row = self.connection.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM exemption_requests WHERE id = ?", (request_id,)
        ).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            raise ValueError(f"未知申请编号: {request_id}")
        return self._request_dict(row)

    @staticmethod
    def _event_dict(event: sqlite3.Row) -> dict:
        return {
            "seq": int(event["seq"]),
            "at": str(event["occurred_at"]),
            "actor": str(event["actor"]),
            "action": str(event["action"]),
            "reason": str(event["reason"]),
            "from_status": (
                None if event["from_status"] is None
                else str(event["from_status"])
            ),
            "to_status": str(event["to_status"]),
        }

    def _request_dict(
        self, row: sqlite3.Row, events: list[dict] | None = None
    ) -> dict:
        """Build one request record, attaching its processing history.

        A list query passes the history it batch-loaded for exactly this
        request (never another request's); when no history is supplied the
        events of this one request are read on demand, which is the path a
        single-request fetch uses. Either way the produced record is
        identical, so list and single views can never drift apart.
        """
        if events is None:
            events = [
                self._event_dict(event)
                for event in self.connection.execute(
                    """
                    SELECT seq, occurred_at, actor, action, reason, from_status,
                           to_status
                    FROM exemption_events
                    WHERE request_id = ?
                    ORDER BY seq
                    """,
                    (str(row["id"]),),
                )
            ]
        return {
            "id": str(row["id"]),
            # Projected from the canonical scope tuple, so the stored scope
            # reads back with the same fields and values the report uses to
            # link the request to its impact record.
            "scope": dict(zip(_SCOPE_FIELDS, self._scope_from_row(row))),
            "applicant": str(row["applicant"]),
            "reason": str(row["reason"]),
            "created_at": str(row["created_at"]),
            "expires_at": str(row["expires_at"]),
            "status": str(row["status"]),
            "decided_at": (
                None if row["decided_at"] is None else str(row["decided_at"])
            ),
            "approver": None if row["approver"] is None else str(row["approver"]),
            "decision_note": (
                None if row["decision_note"] is None
                else str(row["decision_note"])
            ),
            "approved_severity": (
                None if row["approved_severity"] is None
                else str(row["approved_severity"])
            ),
            "revoked_at": (
                None if row["revoked_at"] is None else str(row["revoked_at"])
            ),
            "revoker": None if row["revoker"] is None else str(row["revoker"]),
            "revoke_note": (
                None if row["revoke_note"] is None else str(row["revoke_note"])
            ),
            "events": events,
        }

    def get_exemption(self, request_id: str) -> dict:
        """Return one request with its full processing history."""
        request_id = self._clean_text(request_id, "申请编号")
        return self._fetch_request(request_id)

    def list_exemptions(self, status: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        """List requests (with history), newest first, id as tiebreaker.

        Whatever the status filter (or lack of one), the requests and the
        complete histories attached to the result are read with a fixed
        number of queries: one read selects the matching request rows, and
        one more read loads the history of exactly those requests. The
        history read is scoped to the selected ids, so filtering by status
        never pulls other requests' history in, and the number of reads no
        longer grows with the number of returned requests.
        """
        query = (
            "SELECT * FROM exemption_requests "
            + ("WHERE status = ? " if status is not None else "")
            + "ORDER BY created_at DESC, id ASC"
        )
        parameters: tuple = () if status is None else (status,)
        rows = self.connection.execute(query, parameters).fetchall()
        histories: dict[str, list[dict]] = {str(row["id"]): [] for row in rows}
        if histories:
            # Join against the same selection rather than binding one
            # placeholder per id: this stays a single read with the same one
            # (or zero) status parameter however many requests match, so a
            # large list cannot overflow SQLite's bound-parameter limit, and
            # only the selected requests' events are read.
            event_rows = self.connection.execute(
                """
                SELECT e.request_id, e.seq, e.occurred_at, e.actor, e.action,
                       e.reason, e.from_status, e.to_status
                FROM exemption_events AS e
                JOIN (
                    SELECT id FROM exemption_requests
                """
                + ("WHERE status = ? " if status is not None else "")
                + """
                ) AS r ON r.id = e.request_id
                ORDER BY e.request_id, e.seq
                """,
                parameters,
            )
            for event in event_rows:
                histories[str(event["request_id"])].append(self._event_dict(event))
        return [
            self._request_dict(row, histories[str(row["id"])]) for row in rows
        ]

    def _process_decision(
        self,
        request_id: str,
        handler: str,
        note: str,
        action: str,
        target_status: str,
        when: datetime,
    ) -> dict:
        request_id = self._clean_text(request_id, "申请编号")
        handler = self._clean_text(handler, "处理人")
        note = self._clean_text(note, "处理说明")

        with self._write_tx():
            # Lock the row so two concurrent processes cannot both transition
            # it; the second transaction blocks here and then sees the new
            # status, so exactly one state change is accepted.
            row = self.connection.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM exemption_requests WHERE id = ?",
                (request_id,),
            ).fetchone()
            if row is None:
                raise ValueError(f"未知申请编号: {request_id}")
            current_status = str(row["status"])
            if current_status != EXEMPTION_PENDING:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"只有待审批申请可以{_action_label(action)}，"
                    f"当前状态为{_status_label(current_status)}"
                )
            if format_timestamp(when) >= str(row["expires_at"]):
                raise ValueError("申请已到期，不能再审批")

            approved_severity = None
            if target_status == EXEMPTION_APPROVED:
                if handler == str(row["applicant"]):
                    raise ValueError("申请人不能批准自己的申请")
                # Approval judges the exact stored scope against the current
                # service graph: it must find that one impact record (via its
                # own current dependency path), and records the severity in
                # force now — never the submission-time level, never a
                # same-id record from another source or a manual entry.
                scope = self._scope_from_row(row)
                current_impact = self._current_scope_impact(scope)
                if current_impact is None:
                    raise ValueError("审批时目标影响记录已不存在")
                approved_severity = str(current_impact["severity"])
                cursor = self.connection.execute(
                    """
                    UPDATE exemption_requests
                    SET status = ?, decided_at = ?, approver = ?,
                        decision_note = ?, approved_severity = ?
                    WHERE id = ? AND status = ?
                    """,
                    (
                        target_status, format_timestamp(when), handler, note,
                        approved_severity, request_id, EXEMPTION_PENDING,
                    ),
                )
            else:
                cursor = self.connection.execute(
                    """
                    UPDATE exemption_requests
                    SET status = ?, decided_at = ?, approver = ?,
                        decision_note = ?
                    WHERE id = ? AND status = ?
                    """,
                    (
                        target_status, format_timestamp(when), handler, note,
                        request_id, EXEMPTION_PENDING,
                    ),
                )
            if cursor.rowcount == 0:
                raise ValueError("申请状态已被其他进程改变")
            self._append_event(
                request_id, when, handler, action, note,
                EXEMPTION_PENDING, target_status,
            )
        return self._fetch_request(request_id)

    def approve_exemption(
        self,
        request_id: str,
        handler: str,
        note: str,
        *,
        decided_at: datetime | None = None,
    ) -> dict:
        """Approve a pending request, recording the severity then in force."""
        return self._process_decision(
            request_id, handler, note, "approve", EXEMPTION_APPROVED,
            decided_at or utc_now(),
        )

    def reject_exemption(
        self,
        request_id: str,
        handler: str,
        note: str,
        *,
        decided_at: datetime | None = None,
    ) -> dict:
        """Reject a pending request."""
        return self._process_decision(
            request_id, handler, note, "reject", EXEMPTION_REJECTED,
            decided_at or utc_now(),
        )

    def revoke_exemption(
        self,
        request_id: str,
        handler: str,
        note: str,
        *,
        revoked_at: datetime | None = None,
    ) -> dict:
        """Revoke an approved exemption that has not yet expired."""
        request_id = self._clean_text(request_id, "申请编号")
        handler = self._clean_text(handler, "处理人")
        note = self._clean_text(note, "处理说明")
        when = revoked_at or utc_now()
        if revoked_at is not None:
            if revoked_at.tzinfo is None:
                raise ValueError("撤销时刻必须带有时区信息")
            when = revoked_at.astimezone(timezone.utc)

        with self._write_tx():
            row = self.connection.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM exemption_requests WHERE id = ?",
                (request_id,),
            ).fetchone()
            if row is None:
                raise ValueError(f"未知申请编号: {request_id}")
            status = str(row["status"])
            if status != EXEMPTION_APPROVED:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"只有已批准且未到期的申请可以撤销，"
                    f"当前状态为{_status_label(status)}"
                )
            if format_timestamp(when) >= str(row["expires_at"]):
                raise ValueError("豁免已到期，无需撤销")
            cursor = self.connection.execute(
                """
                UPDATE exemption_requests
                SET status = ?, revoked_at = ?, revoker = ?, revoke_note = ?
                WHERE id = ? AND status = ?
                """,
                (
                    EXEMPTION_REVOKED, format_timestamp(when), handler, note,
                    request_id, EXEMPTION_APPROVED,
                ),
            )
            if cursor.rowcount == 0:
                raise ValueError("申请状态已被其他进程改变")
            self._append_event(
                request_id, when, handler, "revoke", note,
                EXEMPTION_APPROVED, EXEMPTION_REVOKED,
            )
        return self._fetch_request(request_id)

    @staticmethod
    def _inactive_link_reason(
        status: str, expires_at: str, at_text: str
    ) -> str:
        """Why the newest request of a scope is not currently in force.

        Approved-and-unexpired scopes never reach this function; their effect
        depends on the live severity and is decided while the report is built.
        """
        if status == EXEMPTION_PENDING:
            if expires_at <= at_text:
                return f"申请已于 {expires_at} 到期，未获审批"
            return "豁免申请尚在待审批"
        if status == EXEMPTION_REJECTED:
            return "豁免申请已被拒绝"
        if status == EXEMPTION_REVOKED:
            return "豁免已被撤销"
        # An approved request that is not in force can only have expired.
        return f"豁免已于 {expires_at} 到期"

    def _scope_exemption_links(
        self, moment: datetime, service: str | None = None
    ) -> tuple[dict[tuple, dict], dict[tuple, dict]]:
        """Load, in one read, both exemption views the report links against.

        The report used to first fetch every approved-unexpired request and
        then issue another scope lookup for each record without an active
        exemption, so the number of reads grew with the number of output
        records. Every relevant request is now read once here and grouped
        into the two maps the old precedence used:

        * ``active`` — an approved request whose term is in force at
          ``moment`` (the exemption still stops at the expiry instant). When
          several rows qualify for one scope — possible only at a past
          evaluation instant, since a later request cannot be submitted
          until the earlier term has lapsed — the last inserted row wins,
          matching the old unordered scan that overwrote per scope. Whether
          it covers the record is still decided against the current
          severity while the report is built.
        * ``latest`` — the newest request of the scope by the documented
          selection order (submission time newest first, id largest first on
          ties), used only when no approval is in force, together with the
          reason it is not currently covering the record.

        Directory and approval state are always taken at the current moment;
        ``moment`` only judges the term. Rows are confined to ``service``
        when the report is service-scoped; other services' scopes could not
        match the report anyway, but keeping them out also prevents their
        data from being read.
        """
        if service is None:
            rows = self.connection.execute(
                """
                SELECT rowid AS rid, id, service, ecosystem, name, version,
                       vulnerability, matched_name, source, status,
                       expires_at, approved_severity
                FROM exemption_requests
                ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC
                """
            )
        else:
            rows = self.connection.execute(
                """
                SELECT rowid AS rid, id, service, ecosystem, name, version,
                       vulnerability, matched_name, source, status,
                       expires_at, approved_severity
                FROM exemption_requests
                WHERE service = ?
                ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC
                """,
                (service,),
            )
        at_text = format_timestamp(moment)
        latest: dict[tuple, dict] = {}
        active: dict[tuple, dict] = {}
        for row in rows:
            scope = self._scope_from_row(row)
            status = str(row["status"])
            expires_at = str(row["expires_at"])
            # Rows arrive newest first, so the first seen per scope is the
            # documented "latest request" selection; later rows are ignored.
            if scope not in latest:
                latest[scope] = {
                    "id": str(row["id"]),
                    "status": status,
                    "expires_at": expires_at,
                    "approved_severity": (
                        None
                        if row["approved_severity"] is None
                        else str(row["approved_severity"])
                    ),
                    "not_exempt_reason": (
                        None
                        if status == EXEMPTION_APPROVED and expires_at > at_text
                        else self._inactive_link_reason(
                            status, expires_at, at_text
                        )
                    ),
                }
            if status == EXEMPTION_APPROVED and expires_at > at_text:
                candidate = active.get(scope)
                # The old full-table scan saw rows in insertion order and the
                # last inserted approved-unexpired row survived; rowid keeps
                # that choice explicit and deterministic.
                if candidate is None or int(row["rid"]) > candidate["rid"]:
                    active[scope] = {
                        "rid": int(row["rid"]),
                        "id": str(row["id"]),
                        "approved_severity": str(row["approved_severity"]),
                    }
        return active, latest

    def risk_report(
        self,
        service: str | None = None,
        evaluated_at: str | datetime | None = None,
    ) -> dict:
        """Build the JSON risk report.

        Every current impact record is reported with its source, severity,
        direct/indirect flag and dependency path, plus exemption status: the
        linked request and, when an approved exemption is not in force for the
        record, the reason why. Counts and the highest severity consider only
        unexempted records.
        """
        if evaluated_at is None:
            moment = utc_now()
        elif isinstance(evaluated_at, datetime):
            if evaluated_at.tzinfo is None:
                raise ValueError("评估时刻必须带有时区信息")
            moment = evaluated_at.astimezone(timezone.utc)
        else:
            moment = parse_timestamp(evaluated_at, "评估时刻")

        scope_service: str | None = None
        if service is not None:
            scope_service = service.strip()
            if not scope_service:
                raise ValueError("service 不能为空")

        # Build impacts within the selected service only: same-name components,
        # dependencies and exemptions of other services never enter the report,
        # and an unparseable version elsewhere cannot fail this service.
        records = self._impact_records(scope_service)

        # Every exemption request is read once up front (scoped to the
        # selected service, exactly like the impact graph), so request data
        # is no longer queried once per output record.
        active, latest = self._scope_exemption_links(moment, scope_service)
        reported: list[dict] = []
        unexempted_components: set[tuple] = set()
        highest: str | None = None

        for record in records:
            component = record["component"]
            # The scope a request must carry to link to this record is built
            # by the same constructor submission uses, so stored scopes and
            # report records can never drift apart. Dependency paths are not
            # part of the scope: a changed path still links the same request.
            scope = _scope_of_record(record)
            entry = {
                "component": dict(component),
                "vulnerability": record["vulnerability"],
                "source": record["source"],
                "matched_name": record["matched_name"],
                "severity": record["severity"],
                "severity_basis": record["severity_basis"],
                "direct": record["direct"],
                "matched_conditions": record["matched_conditions"],
                "path": [dict(node) for node in record["path"]],
                "exempted": False,
                "exemption_request": None,
                "not_exempt_reason": None,
            }

            exemption = active.get(scope)
            if exemption is not None:
                current_severity = str(record["severity"])
                approved_rank = SEVERITY_RANK[exemption["approved_severity"]]
                if SEVERITY_RANK[current_severity] > approved_rank:
                    # The current rating exceeds what was approved: the
                    # exemption no longer covers this record, but the
                    # approval id stays linked instead of falling back to
                    # "no request".
                    entry["exemption_request"] = exemption["id"]
                    entry["not_exempt_reason"] = (
                        f"当前风险等级 {current_severity} 高于审批时的"
                        f"{exemption['approved_severity']}，超出审批范围"
                    )
                else:
                    entry["exempted"] = True
                    entry["exemption_request"] = exemption["id"]
            else:
                # No approval is in force for the scope: keep linking the
                # newest request (with its pending/rejected/revoked/expired
                # reason); an empty map entry still means no request exists.
                linked = latest.get(scope)
                if linked is not None:
                    entry["exemption_request"] = linked["id"]
                    entry["not_exempt_reason"] = linked["not_exempt_reason"]

            if not entry["exempted"]:
                unexempted_components.add(
                    (
                        component["service"], component["ecosystem"],
                        component["name"], component["version"],
                    )
                )
                if (
                    highest is None
                    or SEVERITY_RANK[record["severity"]] > SEVERITY_RANK[highest]
                ):
                    highest = str(record["severity"])

            reported.append(entry)

        reported.sort(key=_impact_sort_key)

        return {
            "evaluated_at": format_timestamp(moment),
            "service": scope_service,
            "impact_count": len(reported),
            "unhandled_component_count": len(unexempted_components),
            "highest_severity": highest,
            "impacts": reported,
        }


def _status_label(status: str) -> str:
    return {
        EXEMPTION_PENDING: "待审批",
        EXEMPTION_APPROVED: "已批准",
        EXEMPTION_REJECTED: "已拒绝",
        EXEMPTION_REVOKED: "已撤销",
    }.get(status, status)


def _action_label(action: str) -> str:
    return {
        "approve": "批准",
        "reject": "拒绝",
        "revoke": "撤销",
    }.get(action, action)
